# Another LINQ Tool — `.linq` / `.csx` authoring guide

This guide describes the exact `.linq` and `.csx` file format used by the **Another
LINQ Tool** VS Code extension. These files are *not* standard LINQPad `.linq` files or
plain C# script (`.csx`) files — derive behavior only from what is documented here.

Both extensions map to the same language (`linq-csx`) and have identical semantics.
A file is executed by the bundled .NET runner via Roslyn C# scripting.

## File layout

A file is, in order:

1. An **optional metadata header** (see below) that must appear before any C# code.
2. The **C# body**.

The metadata header is one of two mutually-usable styles. Blank lines are allowed
inside it. Header/directive lines are masked before compilation, so they never shift
the line numbers of the C# body (breakpoints stay aligned).

### Style A — LINQPad XML query header

```xml
<Query Kind="Program">
  <Namespace>System</Namespace>
  <Namespace>System.Linq</Namespace>
</Query>
```

- Must start at the beginning of a line and be closed with `</Query>`.
- `Kind` attribute: `Expression`, `Statements`, or `Program`. Missing/empty ⇒ dynamic.
  Any other value is a hard error.
- Each `<Namespace>` element adds a `using` for the body.

### Style B — native directives

One directive per line, optionally prefixed with `//`. Directives must come before the
C# body; parsing stops at the first non-blank, non-directive line.

```csharp
@kind Program
@namespace System.Linq
@profile Northwind
```

- `@kind <Expression|Statements|Program>` — sets the query kind (`@query` is an alias).
- `@namespace <Namespace>` — adds a `using`; repeatable.
- `@profile <name>` — **extension-only** directive. Selects the execution profile for
  this file, overriding the currently-active profile. It is consumed by the extension
  and never reaches the C# compiler. Use the `another-linq-tool_getProfiles` tool to see
  which profile names are valid.

## Query kinds

- **Expression** / **Statements** — run *dynamically* as a C# script and are
  interchangeable. Statements execute top-to-bottom; a final expression on the last line
  **without a trailing semicolon** is captured and displayed as the result.
- **Program** — you must define an entry method `Main` (it may be `void`, return a value,
  be `async Task`, or `async Task<T>`). The runner invokes it automatically. You may
  declare additional types and methods in the file.

## Always-available API

These namespaces are imported implicitly (in addition to profile/`@namespace` imports):
`System`, `System.Linq`, `System.Collections.Generic`, `System.Threading.Tasks`,
`System.Text`, `LinqRunner.Api`.

- `Dump()` — an extension method on any value that renders it inline in the result panel
  with an optional label, e.g. `value.Dump("label")`. It **returns its input**, so it is
  chainable and can be used mid-expression.
- `Db` — present only when the active profile defines a database. It is the profile's
  strongly-typed EF Core `DbContext`, exposed unqualified, e.g. `Db.Customers.Where(...)`.

## Profiles

Execution context is supplied by a **profile** (the active one, or the one named in a
`@profile` directive). A profile can contribute:

- `targetFramework` (`net10.0` / `net11.0`) and optional `efCoreVersion`
- `assemblies` — referenced DLL paths
- `imports` — extra `using` namespaces
- `packages` — NuGet packages restored before running
- `prelude` — C# source prepended to the script body
- an EF Core `DbContext` (`context` type, `provider`, connection string, optional
  context factory) surfaced as `Db`

Connection strings live in VS Code Secret Storage, never in the file or settings JSON.

**Before writing code that depends on profile types, imports, packages, or `Db`, call the
`another-linq-tool_getProfiles` language model tool** to discover the available profiles
and their exact configuration. Do not guess profile names or their contents.
